payload.title: Add secure login to this application.

contract.goal: Implement secure login endpoints for this application, reusing the existing user model and session store
constraints: Reuse the existing SessionStore and UserRepo; do not add a database
Do not add new paid infrastructure or external services
Keep all changes covered by vitest tests under tests/auth/

acceptance_criteria.condition: A valid login credential creates a user session and GET /me returns the user
An expired login credential is rejected with HTTP 401
A login credential cannot be reused after its first successful use
Changes stay within the allowed scope
The whole test suite still passes

contract.goal: Add a minimal login page that submits an email address to the backend login endpoint and shows the result
constraints: Plain HTML and vanilla JavaScript only; no framework, no build step; create the public/ directory if it does not exist
The page must call POST /auth/request with a JSON body {"email": "..."} and display the response message

acceptance_criteria.condition: public/login.html exists and contains a form posting an email to /auth/request
Changes stay within the allowed scope

questions.text: What response format should the page use to display the backend result? Options: (A) parse JSON and display response.message, (B) display the raw response text, or (C) support JSON {message} with raw-text fallback.

How should unsuccessful requests be presented? Options: (A) display the backend message/body for non-2xx responses and a generic message for network/parse errors, (B) display one generic error for every failure, or (C) another specified behavior.

Which login mechanism? The User model has no password field and the repo ships an email stub, and AC-2/AC-3 describe a credential that expires and is single-use. Options: (a) passwordless magic link: POST an email, the app emails a one-time token via EmailSender, the user redeems it to get a session (fits existing code, no model change needed); (b) emailed one-time numeric code (OTP) redeemed with email+code; (c) email+password (would require adding password storage to the user model, which is outside src/auth/** and outside my allowed paths). I recommend (a).

Endpoint names and shapes. Proposed: POST /auth/login with JSON {email} -> 202 {ok:true}; POST /auth/verify with JSON {token} -> 200 {user} and sets the session; POST /auth/logout -> 204 revokes the session; GET /me returns the session's user or 401. Options: (a) accept this proposal; (b) use GET /auth/verify?token=... so the emailed link is clickable directly; (c) other names/paths you prefer (please specify).

How is the session presented to the client? Options: (a) HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/ cookie named `session` (Secure flag only when NODE_ENV=production so local dev works over http); (b) bearer token returned in the JSON body and sent as `Authorization: Bearer <id>`; (c) both. I recommend (a).

Expiry and limits. Proposed defaults: login token expires after 15 minutes, session TTL 7 days, requesting a new token invalidates any earlier unredeemed token for the same email. Options: (a) accept these defaults; (b) different values (please specify).

Response for a login request with an unknown email. Options: (a) return the same 202 as for a known email and send no email (avoids account enumeration); (b) return 404 {error:'user not found'} to match the existing /users/:id style. I recommend (a).

Error codes for redeem failures. Proposed: expired, unknown, already-used or malformed token all return 401 {error:'invalid or expired token'} without distinguishing the cause; malformed request body returns 400. Options: (a) accept; (b) distinguish causes (e.g. 410 for used, 401 for expired). I recommend (a).

Where are pending login tokens stored? Options: (a) a new in-memory TokenStore class under src/auth/ (mirrors SessionStore, honours 'no database'); (b) reuse SessionStore itself for tokens (works but blurs sessions and tokens). I recommend (a). Tokens would be generated with crypto.randomBytes and stored as SHA-256 hashes so a memory dump does not leak live tokens.

response.reason: The contract states the goal as 'secure login' without naming a mechanism, endpoint shapes, session transport, or expiry policy; each of these changes the implementation materially.

answers.answer: (a) email magic link: POST an email, a one-time token is sent via the existing EmailSender and later exchanged for a session. Links expire after 15 minutes and are single-use. No passwords.

interpretation: Create public/login.html as a self-contained plain HTML page with a required email input and submit control.
Intercept form submission in vanilla JavaScript and POST JSON containing exactly the entered email to /auth/request.
Display response.message when the response is JSON with a message, otherwise display its raw text; apply this to successful and non-2xx responses.
Show a generic readable error when the request cannot be completed or its response cannot yield a usable message.
assumptions: A same-origin relative URL /auth/request is correct.
Inline JavaScript and minimal inline CSS are acceptable within public/login.html.
Native browser email validation is sufficient for this minimal page.
risks: The command criterion checks static markers but does not execute browser behavior, so I will add focused UI tests if the repository's existing test setup makes that practical.
A response with neither a JSON message nor non-empty raw text requires a generic fallback.

verification_plan.AC-1: Run the exact contract command, then inspect or test the submit handler to verify POST, Content-Type application/json, exact {email} serialization, and result rendering.
verification_plan.AC-2: Inspect git status and git diff --name-only to confirm every changed path matches public/** or tests/ui/**.

payload.message: Contract v2 accepted after response/error behavior clarification; beginning scoped repository inspection.

interpretation: Add passwordless magic-link login: POST /auth/request with {email} generates a random one-time token, stores only its SHA-256 hash with a 15-minute expiry in a new in-memory TokenStore under src/auth/, and sends the raw token to the user through the existing EmailSender; the response is always 202 {status:'sent', message:'Check your email for a login link'}, whether or not the email is known, and unknown emails get no email.

POST /auth/verify with {token} redeems a valid, unexpired, unused token: it is consumed, a 24-hour session is created in the existing SessionStore for the matching UserRepo user, the session id is set in an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie named `session` (Secure only in production), and the response is 200 {user}.

Any redeem failure (expired, unknown, already used, malformed token) returns 401 {error:'invalid or expired token'}; a malformed JSON body returns 400. Requesting a new link invalidates earlier unredeemed tokens for that email.

GET /me resolves the session cookie through SessionStore and returns 200 with the user, or 401 when there is no valid session; POST /auth/logout revokes the session, clears the cookie and returns 204.

All new code lives in src/auth/** with wiring in src/app.ts; every behaviour is covered by vitest tests under tests/auth/, including the two files named by AC-1 and AC-2, plus a reuse test for AC-3. No database, no new dependencies, no frontend changes.
assumptions: createApp keeps UserRepo as its first argument for backward compatibility and gains an optional second argument with SessionStore, EmailSender, TokenStore, clock and base URL so tests can inject a fake clock and read emails back from MemoryEmailSender; tests/app.test.ts and the other existing tests keep passing unchanged.

The email text contains a link of the form <baseUrl>/auth/verify?token=<raw token> plus the raw token on its own line, so tests can extract it; baseUrl defaults to http://localhost:3000 and is overridable via the createApp options.
Token comparison is done by SHA-256 hashing the presented token and looking it up; tokens are 32 random bytes encoded as base64url.
The existing TODO-backed GET /me handler in src/app.ts is replaced by the session-aware handler.
Production detection for the Secure cookie flag uses NODE_ENV === 'production'.
risks: Cookie sessions without a CSRF token rely on SameSite=Lax; all state-changing endpoints are POST-only, which Lax protects against cross-site form posts in modern browsers.
In-memory token and session stores are lost on restart, consistent with the existing SessionStore design.
The frontend task depends on the exact /auth/request response shape; I will match the clarified shape verbatim.
AC-3 is human-reviewed; I will add an explicit vitest reuse test so the reviewer has runnable evidence.

verification_plan.AC-1: Write tests/auth/valid-login.test.ts: POST /auth/request for a seeded user, read the token from MemoryEmailSender.sent, POST /auth/verify, assert 200 with the user and a Set-Cookie `session` header with HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax, then GET /me with that cookie and assert 200 with the same user. Run `npx vitest run tests/auth/valid-login.test.ts` and confirm it passes.
verification_plan.AC-2: Write tests/auth/expired-login.test.ts using an injected clock: request a link, advance the clock past 15 minutes, POST /auth/verify and assert HTTP 401 with {error:'invalid or expired token'} and no session cookie, and assert GET /me is still 401. Run `npx vitest run tests/auth/expired-login.test.ts` and confirm it passes.
verification_plan.AC-3: Write tests/auth/reuse-login.test.ts: redeem a token once (200), redeem the same token again and assert 401 and no new session cookie; also assert that requesting a new link invalidates the previous one. Run it and confirm by reading src/auth code that the token is deleted from the store before a session is created.
verification_plan.AC-4: Run `git status --porcelain` and `git diff --name-only` before submitting and confirm every changed path matches src/auth/**, src/app.ts or tests/auth/**.
verification_plan.AC-5: Run `npx vitest run` for the full suite and `npm run typecheck`, and confirm both exit 0 with no failures.

payload.message: Added scoped UI contract tests for required email input, POST endpoint/body, and message rendering.
Implemented public/login.html with accessible form, JSON POST, JSON-message/raw-text response handling, and readable failure fallback.
All checks green: exact AC-1 command passed, 22/22 repository tests passed, typecheck passed, and changed paths are limited to public/** and tests/ui/**.

AC-1.note: Ran the exact grep command successfully; focused Vitest assertions also verified required email input, POST /auth/request, JSON Content-Type/body, and response message rendering.

AC-2.note: git status --short lists only public/ and tests/ui/, both permitted by scope.allowed_paths.

submission.summary: Created a minimal self-contained login page and UI contract tests. The page sends {email} as JSON, prefers JSON response.message with raw-text fallback, displays backend non-2xx bodies, and shows a readable generic network/empty-response error. Exact acceptance command, full test suite (22/22), focused tests (2/2), and TypeScript typecheck all passed.

payload.message: Tests written under tests/auth/ (6 files, 29 tests), TokenStore + magic-link routes implemented in src/auth/, wired into src/app.ts. Checks green: AC-1, AC-2 and reuse tests pass individually, full suite 59/59, tsc --noEmit clean. Changed paths: src/app.ts, src/auth/**, tests/auth/** only.

AC-1.note: npx vitest run tests/auth/valid-login.test.ts: 5/5 passed. Covers request -> emailed token -> POST /auth/verify 200 {user} + Set-Cookie session (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/) -> GET /me 200 {user}; also asserts the session exists in SessionStore for the user.

AC-2.note: npx vitest run tests/auth/expired-login.test.ts: 4/4 passed. With an injected clock, a token presented 15min+1ms after issue gets 401 {error:'invalid or expired token'} and no cookie; exact 15min boundary still accepted; expired session on /me returns 401.

AC-3.note: For human review: tests/auth/reuse-login.test.ts (4/4 passed) redeems a token twice and asserts second use is 401 with no new cookie, that the store is empty after redemption, and that requesting a new link invalidates the earlier one. Mechanism: TokenStore.redeem() deletes the hash entry before returning the user id (src/auth/token-store.ts), so a session is only created for the first presentation.

AC-4.note: git status --porcelain shows only: M src/app.ts, ?? src/auth/ (magic-link.ts, token-store.ts), ?? tests/auth/ (helpers.ts, valid-login, expired-login, reuse-login, request-login, session, token-store tests). All within scope.allowed_paths. Changes are uncommitted in the worktree on branch relay/t-backend-auth.

AC-5.note: npx vitest run: 11 files, 59/59 tests passed (existing 30 + 29 new). npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit) clean.

submission.summary: Passwordless magic-link login per the clarified contract. POST /auth/request {email} -> 202 {status:'sent', message:'Check your email for a login link'} for known and unknown emails alike; for known users a 32-byte base64url token is issued (SHA-256 hash stored in a new in-memory TokenStore, 15-minute TTL, earlier tokens for that user invalidated) and emailed via the existing EmailSender as <baseUrl>/auth/verify?token=... POST /auth/verify {token} consumes the token, creates a 24h session in the existing SessionStore, sets an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax Path=/ cookie named `session` (Secure only when NODE_ENV=production or secureCookies option), and returns 200 {user}; all redeem failures return 401 {error:'invalid or expired token'}, malformed bodies 400. POST /auth/logout revokes and clears the cookie -> 204. GET /me resolves the cookie -> 200 {user} or 401 {error:'not authenticated'}. createApp keeps UserRepo as first arg and gains an optional options object (sessions, tokens, emails, baseUrl, secureCookies) for injection; no new dependencies, no DB, no frontend changes. Files: src/auth/token-store.ts, src/auth/magic-link.ts, src/app.ts, tests/auth/*.

payload.observed_failure: Manual test: redeeming the same token twice returned 200 both times and created two sessions; expected 401 on the second redeem.

repair.observed_failure: AC-3: Manual test: redeeming the same token twice returned 200 both times and created two sessions; expected 401 on the second redeem.
repair.requested_correction: Make the following criteria pass without touching unrelated code: A login credential cannot be reused after its first successful use

payload.reason: Cannot reproduce the AC-3 failure. Redeeming the same token twice returns 200 then 401 with exactly one session, both via Hono's in-process request helper (tests/auth/reuse-login.test.ts) and over a real listening @hono/node-server (new tests/auth/http-reuse.test.ts, plus a manual tsx script). TokenStore.redeem deletes the hash before returning, so a second redeem cannot find it. Please tell me how the manual test was run: (1) which server/command and which branch or worktree (this code lives in worktree branch relay/t-backend-auth; main has no /auth routes at all), (2) how the token was obtained, since the default MemoryEmailSender does not print emails, so `npm start` gives a manual tester no way to see a token, and (3) whether the second redeem used POST /auth/verify with JSON {token} or the emailed GET link. If the problem is that tokens are unobservable when running the server, I can add a dev-only email sender under src/auth/ that logs the login link to stdout when NODE_ENV is not production, so a reviewer can complete the manual test; say so and I will add it.

payload.message: You are right, my observation was from a stale server process. Your reuse test is sufficient: keep tests/auth/reuse-login.test.ts and resubmit without changing production code.

AC-1.note: npx vitest run tests/auth/valid-login.test.ts: 5/5 passed (unchanged since attempt 1).

AC-2.note: npx vitest run tests/auth/expired-login.test.ts: 4/4 passed (unchanged since attempt 1).

AC-3.note: Reviewer confirmed the attempt-1 observation came from a stale server process. No production code changed. Evidence: tests/auth/reuse-login.test.ts (4/4) asserts second redeem -> 401, no new cookie, store empty after redemption, new request invalidates old link. Added tests/auth/http-reuse.test.ts (1/1), which boots a real @hono/node-server and redeems the same token twice over HTTP: first 200, second 401, exactly one session in SessionStore. Mechanism: TokenStore.redeem deletes the token hash before returning the user id (src/auth/token-store.ts).

AC-4.note: git status --porcelain: M src/app.ts, ?? src/auth/ (magic-link.ts, token-store.ts), ?? tests/auth/ (8 files). All within allowed paths. Only change since attempt 1 is the new test file tests/auth/http-reuse.test.ts.

AC-5.note: npx vitest run: 12 files, 60/60 passed. npm run typecheck clean.

submission.summary: Resubmission for repair r1 (AC-3). Per the reviewer's reply, the double-200 observation was from a stale server process; production code is unchanged from attempt 1. Added one HTTP-level regression test (tests/auth/http-reuse.test.ts) that reproduces the manual test against a real listening server and proves the second redeem returns 401 with a single session. Implementation summary unchanged: POST /auth/request, POST /auth/verify, POST /auth/logout, GET /me; TokenStore stores SHA-256 hashes with 15-minute TTL and single-use redemption; sessions live 24h in the existing SessionStore behind an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie.
